newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Minera Aurifera to invest $15 mln in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Minera Aurifera to invest $15 mln in 1997.

text.p: Peru's second largest gold-miner Minera Aurifera Retamas SA plans to invest $15 million this year on exploration in the north of the country.

"The program we have is for $15 million to develop explorations at gold reserves in the regions of La Libertad, Cajamarca and Piura," Retamas president Andres Marsano told Reuters. He added that Retamas, which produces its gold from the same northern region, expected to raise output this year to 4.5 tonnes from 3.9 tonnes in 1996.

Although Peru's second largest gold company, Retamas is dwarfed by Minera Yanacocha SA, the biggest gold mine in South America. Yanacocha, in the northern Andes, produced about 40 percent of Peru's total 1996 gold output of 64.8 tonnes. It is owned by partners Newmont Gold Co and local firm Cia. Minera Buenaventura SA, which have 51.35 percent and 43.65 percent respectively.

Marsano added that Retamas would seek a foreign partner to help develop projects once its exploratory studies had been completed. "In mining, you have to be tremendously conservative ... what we want is to have all the geological studies so as to negotiate after knowing what we have," he said.
